chunks: And as for what Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from Abu Ja'far, from al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)
regarding a person in ihram who looked at his wife with desire and emitted semen, he said: There is no penalty upon him.

The correct interpretation of this report is that we understand it as referring to the state of heedlessness and forgetfulness, because whoever looks while heedless or forgetful looks with desire and emits semen, there is no penalty upon him, just as if he had intercourse while forgetful, no expiation would be incumbent upon him, as we have clarified in our book Al-Kabir.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a person in ihram who looks at their spouse and emits semen due to forgetfulness?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies that the exemption from penalty applies specifically when the gaze and subsequent emission occur in a state of heedlessness (sahw) or forgetfulness, distinguishing it from deliberate acts. This interpretation aligns with the broader Shia legal principle that minor sins or ritual breaches committed unintentionally do not incur the full expiation (kaffarah) required for intentional violations.
